recent_articles.title: 39 Hardinge Road: The Reason Why Rabri Devi Doesn't Want To Vacate Bungalow
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rabri Devi**, former Bihar chief minister, has refused to vacate her 10 Circular Road bungalow in Patna despite an eviction notice from the **Bihar government**. The state government has allocated her a new house on Hardinge Road, but she remains adamant and claims superstition is behind her resistance.  The property has been a symbol of her political career for over two decades and is now being contested by the government.

recent_articles.title: Bihar MLC polls: NDA eyes 9 seats as political heirs enter the race | India News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Several prominent figures in Bihar are vying for the 10 MLC seats up for election on June 18th. **Nishant Kumar**, son of former CM **Nitish Kumar**, and **Deepak Prakash**, son of RLM chief **Upendra Kushwaha**, are expected to secure berths from their respective parties, while **Chirag Paswan** must choose among his nephew **Seemant Mrinal**, brother-in-law **Ved Prakash Pandey**, and former MLC **Hulash Pandey**.  **Jitan Ram Manjhi** is reportedly seeking a seat for his son **Praveen Kumar Suman**, who is already an MLC and minister. The RJD faces a dilemma between choosing **Tej Pratap Yadav**, **Rohini Acharya**, or outgoing party member **Sunil Singh**.

recent_articles.title: Bihar MLC polls: NDA eyes 9 seats as political heirs enter the race | India News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Several prominent figures are vying for the 10 Bihar MLC seats up for election on June 18th. **Nishant Kumar**, son of former CM **Nitish Kumar**, and **Deepak Prakash**, son of RLM chief and Rajya Sabha MP **Upendra Kushwaha**, are expected to secure berths from their respective parties.  **Chirag Paswan**, leader of the LJP(RV) and Union cabinet minister, must choose among his nephew **Seemant Mrinal**, brother-in-law **Ved Prakash Pandey**, and former MLC **Hulash Pandey**. **Jitan Ram Manjhi**, HAM(S) chief and Union cabinet minister, is reportedly seeking a seat for his son **Praveen Kumar Suman**.  The RJD faces a dilemma between choosing **Tej Pratap Yadav** or **Rohini Acharya** as a potential candidate.

recent_articles.title: Abhishek Banerjee attack: Can Mamata Banerjee rebuild INDIA bloc after TMC poll rout? - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The attack on **Abhishek Banerjee**, nephew of **Mamata Banerjee**, has sparked unexpected support for her from across the Opposition, including **Rahul Gandhi** and **Mallikarjun Kharge**.  This show of solidarity, despite past tensions between the **Trinamool Congress** and other parties like the **Congress**, raises questions about the future of the fractured **INDIA bloc** and its potential to challenge the BJP. The attack has also highlighted the vulnerability of the **Trinamool Congress** after a devastating defeat in the Bengal Assembly elections.

recent_articles.title: Let Them Evict Me By Force, I Won't Vacate: Rabri Devi On Bihar Residence, RJD, Bungalow Row, Samrat Choudhary
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rabri Devi**, former chief minister of Bihar and leader of the opposition, has refused to vacate her government-allotted bungalow at 10 Circular Road despite an order from the building construction department to move. The order was issued in May to **Nand Kishor Ram**, the Dairy and Fisheries Minister in the NDA government.  **Leshi Singh**, the minister for building construction, stated that the previous order allotting the house to **Rabri Devi** remains valid and she should relocate to 39, Hardinge Road. The situation has sparked controversy with RJD spokesperson **Chittaranjan Gagan** accusing the ruling NDA of targeting opposition leaders.

recent_articles.title: Abhishek Banerjee heckled | TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee allegedly manhandled by agitating locals at Sonarpur in Bengal's South 24 Parganas: Police - Telegraph India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Abhishek Banerjee**, **Trinamool Congress** national general secretary, was physically attacked by a mob in Sonarpur, West Bengal, while visiting families of post-poll violence victims.  The incident occurred after he arrived to meet the family of Sanju Karmakar, a victim of the violence.  Local residents shouted "thief" slogans and hurled objects at him. **Derek O'Brien**, leader of Trinamool in Rajya Sabha, condemned the attack and called for action from the police. Opposition leaders across parties, including **Samik Bhattacharya** (BJP), **Mallikarjun Kharge** (Congress), **Akhilesh Yadav** (SP), **Arvind Kejriwal** (AAP), and **Tejashwi Yadav** (RJD), condemned the attack on Banerjee and called for an end to political violence.

recent_articles.title: Bihar CM woos investors with amended package, says govt.’s top priority is ensuring safety - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, the Chief Minister of Bihar, emphasized the government's commitment to ensuring the security of businessmen and boosting industrial growth in the state. He inaugurated a business conclave organized by the **Bihar Chamber of Commerce and Industries** to mark its centenary year. The CM highlighted the "Bihar Industrial Investment Promotion Package-2025" aimed at attracting private investment, while assuring investors that their safety is paramount. Choudhary also addressed concerns about crime and caste politics, stating that criminals are not defined by their background and the government will prioritize investor security.

recent_articles.title: Setback for NDA as RJD wins MLC byelection in Bihar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)** won the Bhojpur-Buxar Legislative Council seat in a byelection, defeating the **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)** candidate. **Sonu Rai**, representing the RJD, secured victory with 2,486 votes, while his opponent, **Kanhaiya Prasad** of the JD(U), received 2,146 votes. The RJD has attributed their win to alleged manipulation and fraud in the electoral process.

recent_articles.title: Nitish and BJP have no moral right to speak on dynastic politics, says Tejashwi Yadav - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tejashwi Yadav**, leader of the opposition in Bihar's Legislative Assembly, criticized **Nitish Kumar** and **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** for their involvement in dynasty politics following the expansion of the **Bihar Cabinet**.  Yadav argued that both the **BJP** and its allies are engaging in dynasty politics, citing examples like the inclusion of sons of former Chief Ministers in the new cabinet.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: IUML enters new era as Fathima Thahiliya becomes first woman MLA - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Fathima Thahiliya**, a former Haritha leader and practicing lawyer, has become the first woman from the **Indian Union Muslim League (IUML)** to be elected to the Kerala Assembly.  She defeated **T.P. Ramakrishnan**, the LDF convener, by a significant margin of 5,087 votes. This victory marks a turning point for the IUML, which had previously faced criticism for its lack of female representation in public life. The party's leadership has increasingly embraced women's participation in politics, as evidenced by their decision to field two women candidates this election.  While Ms. Thahiliya's win is a significant step forward, it also signals the potential for broader acceptance of women within the IUML's electoral framework.

recent_articles.title: BJP attacking Bengali culture, pride: Kejriwal; Modi won’t have his way in Bengal: Tejashwi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Arvind Kejriwal**, former Delhi Chief Minister and convener of the **Aam Aadmi Party**, joined the Trinamool Congress campaign in West Bengal on Sunday, addressing three rallies in Kolkata and Howrah.  His visit coincides with the final days of campaigning for the second phase of the Assembly elections, scheduled to conclude Monday evening. The AAP recently experienced a setback as seven of its MPs switched to the **Bharatiya Janata Party**.

recent_articles.title: Election Commission, and not the BJP, seems to be fighting Trinamool in West Bengal, says Kapil Sibal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kapil Sibal**, a senior Supreme Court lawyer and Rajya Sabha MP, criticized the **Election Commission of India (ECI)**'s actions in West Bengal ahead of the upcoming elections. He accused the **EC** and the **BJP** of working together to suppress the Trinamool Congress (TMC), alleging an "unconstitutional Emergency" and a disproportionate deployment of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF).  Other opposition leaders, including **Arvind Kejriwal**, have also expressed concern over the situation.

recent_articles.title: Poll bugle to fall silent across Tamil Nadu on Tuesday evening - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Political parties** in Tamil Nadu are concluding their intense campaigning ahead of the Assembly election on April 23rd.  Polling will begin at 7 a.m. that day, with all political functionaries and party workers not eligible to vote required to vacate the area by 6 p.m. on Tuesday. **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Rahul Gandhi**, and other prominent leaders from various parties have campaigned in the state, while the Chief Electoral Officer has outlined strict regulations for the period leading up to the election.  These include restrictions on public gatherings, vehicle usage, and the establishment of polling booths.

recent_articles.title: ​A plan of change: On Bihar politics and the BJP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, a former member of the Rashtriya Janata Dal and Janata Dal (United), was sworn in as the 24th Chief Minister of Bihar on April 15, 2026.  This marks the first time a politician from the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** has held the office. The BJP's strategy for growth involved outgrowing regional partners and shifting power dynamics within the state, culminating in Choudhary's appointment after years of maneuvering.  The move signifies a shift in Bihar's political landscape as the BJP seeks to solidify its hold on the OBC-EBC base that was previously held by **Nitish Kumar**.

recent_articles.title: Bihar CM slams opposition over women's quota bill - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary** criticized the opposition parties for their refusal to support an amendment to the women's reservation bill, calling it a "black day" and vowing retaliation. **Sanjay Saraogi**, state party president of the BJP, announced that the party's women's wing would hold a protest on April 20th against the opposition's stance. The amendment, which grants 33% reservation to women in Parliament, was passed by an overwhelming majority in 2023 but faced opposition from non-NDA parties who were wary of its link with delimitation.

recent_articles.title: It’ a red-letter day, says Revanth; KTR blames BJP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the defeat of the Women's Reservation Bill in Parliament, **Congress** and **Bharatiya Rashtra Samithi (BRS)** leaders praised opposition parties for uniting to block the controversial legislation.  **Rahul Gandhi**, **Mallikarjun Kharge**, and **A. Revanth Reddy** led the charge against the bill, with **K. T. Rama Rao** blaming the BJP for its failure. **Bandi Sanjay** accused the Congress of using the bill to weaken southern India, while **N Ramchander Rao** criticized the bill's defeat as a setback for women's empowerment.

recent_articles.title: Beneath the euphoria, Bihar’s first BJP Chief Minister faces several significant challenges - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Newly sworn-in **Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary**, a former Deputy Chief Minister in the previous Nitish Kumar government, faces significant challenges as he assumes leadership of Bihar.  **Choudhary**, who joined the BJP in 2017 after a career in opposition parties, must navigate complex coalition dynamics and match the political persona of his predecessor while managing high expectations from the people. He also needs to address financial mismanagement, communal harmony concerns, and doubts about his abilities within the BJP and its ideological parent organization, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS).  **Choudhary** will need to establish his administrative capabilities in a state known for groupism among bureaucrats and broaden the BJP's voter base while maintaining alliances with existing parties.

recent_articles.title: Samrat Choudhary sworn in as Bihar’s first BJP CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Samrat Choudhary**, newly elected leader of the **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)**, was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Bihar on Wednesday.  He was accompanied by two senior JD(U) leaders, **Bijendra Prasad Yadav** and **Vijay Kumar Choudhary**, who are expected to serve as Deputy CMs. The swearing-in ceremony took place at Lok Bhawan with prominent figures from the BJP and former CM Nitish Kumar in attendance.  The new government is expected to expand after the results of upcoming state elections.

recent_articles.title: INDIA bloc opposes Delimitation Bill - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mallikarjun Kharge**, president of the **All India Congress Committee (AICC)**, announced that the INDIA bloc has unanimously decided to oppose the Delimitation Bill.  **Kharge** stated that opposition parties are not against the Women’s Reservation Bill but are concerned about the bill's linking with delimitation and seat increases in State Assemblies. Several Opposition leaders, including **T.R. Baalu**, **Tejashwi Yadav**, and **Sanjay Raut**, expressed their opposition to the Delimitation Bill.

recent_articles.title: Noida workers’ protests: Two RJD spokespersons booked for sharing ‘misleading’ video, inciting tension - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)** spokespersons **Priyanka Bharti** and **Kanchana Yadav** have been accused of sharing a video from Madhya Pradesh on social media, falsely linking it to the ongoing labor protests in Noida.  They are also being investigated for inciting tension by posting about the incident on X and Facebook. The **Uttar Pardesh Police** have registered an FIR against them and the X handle @ItsKtyni, alleging they spread rumors during the protests.

recent_articles.title: Bihar political history timeline: 1990 to 2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nitish Kumar**, the long-serving Chief Minister of Bihar, is set to resign on April 14, 2026, after a two-decade tenure.  Kumar's resignation follows his successful re-election as Chief Minister in 2025 and his nomination for the Rajya Sabha. The BJP will appoint its first Chief Minister in the state, marking a significant shift in Bihar's political landscape. Kumar's departure opens the door for a new chapter in Bihar's governance.

recent_articles.title: Double murder in Bihar, but BJP, JD(U) vying for CM seat: Tejashwi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tejashwi Yadav**, leader of the **Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)**, criticized the ruling **BJP** and **Janata Dal (United)** for their focus on a Chief Minister seat while lawlessness prevails in Bihar.  He condemned a double murder in Araria, alleging police inaction and highlighting rising crime rates under the current government. Yadav urged the government to prioritize youth aspirations and fulfill teacher recruitment promises.

recent_articles.title: In Bihar, the prohibition law has become a joke, says Tejashwi Yadav - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tejashwi Yadav**, leader of the **opposition** in Bihar, criticized the state government's 10-year prohibition policy, accusing it of being "institutional corruption" and enabling a multi-billion rupee illegal liquor market. He cited data showing an increase in seizures and consumption despite the law's implementation, alleging that the government has failed to curb illicit liquor trade and instead is promoting corruption. **Yadav** also pointed out that the prohibition policy has disproportionately targeted poor communities and led to deaths from spurious liquor.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Close contest likely across Wayanad’s three constituencies - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: As Wayanad prepares for the April 9 Assembly elections, local issues are expected to dominate the campaign. **Priyanka Gandhi Vadra**, **Congress** general secretary and representative of the Wayanad Lok Sabha segment, is seeking re-election in a district where voters prioritize local candidates and concerns. The aftermath of the 2024 Mundakkai–Chooralmala landslides has become a key issue in Kalpetta, while tribal land rights and welfare remain central to the contests in Mananthavady and Sulthan Bathery.  The UDF is banking on its traditional support base and anti-incumbency sentiment, while the LDF emphasizes governance, welfare delivery, and crisis response. The BJP is attempting to expand its presence.

recent_articles.title: Tejashwi challenges Bihar CM, deputy CMs for a public debate over State’s progress - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tejashwi Yadav**, leader of the **Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)**, criticized the **Nitish Kumar-led NDA government** in Bihar, claiming it has failed to improve various sectors.  He cited statistics showing low literacy rates, income levels, and investment compared to other states. He also pointed out high crime rates, poverty, unemployment, and pollution levels. The **BJP** and **JD(U)** defended the government's record, arguing that Bihar has flourished under their leadership.

recent_articles.title: LDF corrected course after setback, confident of minority support, says RJD State secretary general Varughese George - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)** is contesting three seats in the upcoming Kerala Assembly elections, prioritizing a generational shift with senior leaders stepping aside.  The party's candidate for Vadakara constituency is a well-known local leader who has served as the Eramala grama panchayat president three times. **RJD** believes its support base remains strong and anticipates consolidating traditional socialist votes in the region. The party, while facing internal issues, maintains it is united and confident of securing victory.

recent_articles.title: CAG flags ₹3.69 lakh crore cess transfer shortfall; RJD MP demands accountability in Rajya Sabha - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A **Rajya Sabha** member from the **Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)**, A.D. Singh, raised concerns about significant shortfalls in the transfer of cess collections to designated funds, citing a **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) report**. The report revealed lapses spanning five decades, with as much as ₹3.69 lakh crore remaining un-transferred between FY 2023-24 and earlier years.  Singh highlighted specific instances of shortfalls in the Oil Industry Development Board, health and education sectors, Investor Education and Protection Fund, and Monetisation of National Highways Fund. He also pointed to discrepancies in official accounts, demanding immediate corrective action from the government.

recent_articles.title: The burden of the new Bihar Chief Minister - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bihar** is set to elect a new Chief Minister after **Nitish Kumar** stepped down, marking the end of his 20-year rule. The change signifies a shift in power from the RJD to the BJP, with Delhi now calling the shots for the first time since 1990.  The incoming Chief Minister will face challenges in maintaining communal harmony and addressing Bihar's high migration rate while navigating potential social anxieties over reservation policies. While the Congress could potentially fill the vacuum left by the JD(U), its future success hinges on breaking free from the RJD's shadow.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly elections: Full list of LDF candidates - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Left Democratic Front (LDF) has released its complete list of candidates for the upcoming Kerala Legislative Assembly election. The CPI(M) fielded a strong lineup led by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, with prominent ministerial presence and several Independents supporting the LDF.  The CPI also renominated all four of its incumbent Ministers.

recent_articles.title: Bihar will remain indebted to Nitish Kumar for building a ‘New Bihar’: Nitin Nabin - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nitin Nabin**, **Nitish Kumar**, and the **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)** celebrated the conclusion of the fifth phase of the "Samriddhi Yatra" in Patna.  **Nabin** praised **Kumar's** leadership for transforming Bihar from a state of despair into one of development, highlighting the government's achievements in electricity access and improved living standards. He also expressed gratitude to Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** for supporting the NDA's efforts in Bihar. The "Samriddhi Yatra" was launched on March 10th and concluded with **Kumar** inaugurating projects worth ₹2183 crore.

recent_articles.title: CAG empanelled auditors to audit urban local bodies (ULBs): Bihar Deputy CM Vijay Sinha - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bihar**'s government has decided to audit all urban local bodies (ULBs) using **CAG** empanelled auditors. Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Kumar Sinha stated that this decision is a part of the state's zero-tolerance policy towards corruption and aims to improve transparency in governance. The auditing will be conducted according to National Municipal Accounts Manual provisions and cover 19 municipal corporations, 89 municipal councils, and 154 nagar panchayats.  The government also plans to develop new townships and redevelop existing ones to promote urbanisation and provide "clean city, green city" initiatives.

recent_articles.title: Transgender bill passed by voice vote in Lok Sabha - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Lok Sabha** passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026, by voice vote. The bill aims to redefine "transgender person" based on biological or physiological markers and socio-cultural identities, while opposition parties like the Congress, DMK, and SP argued that it violates basic human rights and undermines self-determination.  The government defended the bill as necessary for providing safety and benefits to the transgender community.

recent_articles.title: Delhi HC dismisses Lalu Yadav's plea to quash CBI FIR in land-for-jobs case - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Delhi High Court** dismissed a petition by former Bihar Chief Minister and RJD supremo **Lalu Prasad Yadav** to quash the FIR in the land-for-jobs case. The court ruled that the petition lacked merit and dismissed it, leaving the case against **Yadav**, his family members, and others related to alleged land deals during his tenure as Railway Minister.  The case involves appointments made in the West Central Zone of Indian Railways between 2004 and 2009.

recent_articles.title: Opposition MPs, activists oppose amendments to Transgender Persons Act - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Members of Parliament and political party officials from across the country voiced strong opposition to a proposed amendment to the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, at a public hearing in New Delhi.  **Rajya Sabha MPs** from various parties, including the **Rashtriya Janata Dal**, **Indian National Congress**, and the **Communist Party of India (Marxist)**, criticized the Bill's removal of transgender people's right to self-perceived gender identity and its introduction of a medical board for determining transgender status.  They argued that the government's actions were regressive and feared public backlash.

recent_articles.title: Opposition MPs, activists oppose amendments to Transgender Persons Act - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Members of Parliament** and officials from various political parties voiced strong opposition to the **Union government’s** proposed amendment to the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.  At a public hearing held at the Press Club of India, **Rajya Sabha MPs** from the Rashtriya Janata Dal, Indian National Congress, and the Communist Party of India (Marxist) criticized the Bill's attempt to remove self-perceived gender identity recognition and introduce a medical board for determining transgender status.  They expressed concerns about the government’s motives and the potential impact on trans rights. The **Bill**, introduced in the Lok Sabha by **Union Social Justice Minister Virendra Kumar**, has drawn criticism from both trans communities and LGBTQ+ groups, who argue that it undermines the Act's purpose of protecting genuine transgender individuals.
